claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1.
A thin alumina-forming surface coating should be applied to the alloy by CVD, PVD, or pack cementation.
The coating will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 barrier layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 film will isolate the HfNbTaTiZr substrate from oxygen.
Isolating the substrate from oxygen will minimize oxidation-driven degradation.
The surface coating will not alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical performance.
At about 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours, coated specimens will exhibit less oxidation than uncoated specimens, as indicated by lower weight gain.
After exposure, coated specimens will show no internal oxide penetration.
Coated specimens will retain room-temperature ductility comparable to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Coated specimens will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at quasi-static strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
High-temperature oxygen exposure degrades the mechanical performance of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr over time.
Prolonged thermal exposure may impair coating adhesion.
Thermal stresses or cyclic loading may cause coating spallation and thereby compromise oxidation resistance and mechanical performance.
